teaser.text: Alphabet is the company behind Google, and its business begins with a free service: helping people find information and get things done. It turns that daily activity into money from advertising, subscriptions, computing, digital goods, devices and newer ventures.

stock.title: Alphabet stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Alphabet’s stock forecast spans bear, base, bull and weighted scenarios, with cash generation and AI investment driving the range.
stock.opening: Alphabet’s weighted case reaches US$510.69 by October 2029, a 46% return including dividends. Alphabet’s upside depends on turning AI and infrastructure investment into durable cash per share.
stock.closing: The full Alphabet memo answers how Alphabet’s business works, who its rivals are, how management is allocating capital, and what risks could change the view.

blocks.heading: Where could Alphabet's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to $376.88 in October 2027, $429.30 in October 2028 and $510.69 in October 2029, including dividends. Those prices imply returns of 7%, 23% and 46% from today’s $351.66. By October 2029, however, the bear case reaches only $238.70 while the bull case reaches $792.61, so the path matters as much as the average.
The probabilities are 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull. The base case therefore carries most weight, but the downside is substantial if Search economics weaken before Cloud returns become visible.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Alphabet?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the main operating judgement. The latest proxy is about $174,800 million, based on trailing operating income plus annualised first-half depreciation. The base case rises to $206,700 million in October 2027, then $240,950 million and $276,000 million, as Search, YouTube, subscriptions and Cloud grow. Cloud revenue grew 82% year over year and backlog reached about $513,900 million, but infrastructure spending limits early margin expansion.

The bear case keeps EBITDA near the latest proxy before reaching $187,200 million, because AI answers may reduce valuable clicks, serving costs may rise and Cloud conversion may lag. The bull case reaches $331,800 million as AI supports Search, backlog converts quickly and new capacity earns attractive margins. These are estimates, not guidance. Management raised 2026 capital-spending guidance to $195,000–$205,000 million and signalled another significant increase in 2027.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Alphabet really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations minus spending on long-lasting assets. In 2025, Alphabet generated $164,713 million from operations and spent $91,447 million on capital spending, leaving $73,266 million of free cash flow. Capital spending absorbed almost the entire increase in operating cash, so free-cash-flow margin fell to 18.2%.

dividend.title: Alphabet dividend: payments, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: Alphabet's dividend payments, cash coverage, possible changes and current yield, explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Alphabet paid $0.83 per share in 2025, with the forecast rising to $1.10, $1.40 and $1.70 in the base case. Its cash has funded dividends and much larger buybacks, but negative second-quarter free cash flow makes a dividend freeze credible.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Alphabet's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Alphabet pay its shareholders?

paragraphs.text: The dividend rises from the 2025 rate of $0.83 to $1.10, $1.40 and $1.70 in the base case. The bear case freezes it because capital spending is high; the bull case reaches $2.30 as cash conversion improves. The freeze remains credible because second-quarter free cash flow was negative $5,855 million.

blocks.heading: Is Alphabet's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Alphabet returned most free cash flow through buybacks, with dividends beginning in 2024. A payout can exceed cash free after capital expenditure because employee share awards create an economic cost without requiring cash at the moment of grant. Buybacks reduce the share count, but new employee shares replace part of that reduction.

Stock compensation saves cash today but gives employees part of the company. Alphabet recorded $24,953 million of it in 2025. Subtracting that owner cost leaves approximately $48,313 million of real free cash flow. Buybacks can offset employee issuance, but counting all buybacks and stock compensation as separate costs can double-count dilution.

blocks.heading: What is Alphabet's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash after capital expenditure. Alphabet’s recent free-cash-flow yield is only a small current return on the share price, and its real free-cash-flow yield is thinner still. That compares poorly with the 5.24% ten-year Treasury yield, so investors are relying heavily on future growth rather than current cash.

earnings.title: Alphabet earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Alphabet's next results are expected October 28, 2026; see guidance, recent results and the Cloud costs to watch.
earnings.opening: Alphabet's next results are expected on October 28, 2026. Watch whether rented computing capacity becomes a lasting margin burden.
earnings.closing: The full memo answers what else matters about Alphabet's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: On July 22, management raised 2026 capital-expenditure guidance to US$195,000 million–US$205,000 million. Capital expenditure, or CapEx, means buying long-lived assets such as servers, networking equipment and data centers. Management said capacity is arriving sooner than expected and signalled another significant increase in 2027.

blocks.heading: Has Alphabet kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The earlier bargain worked as promised: Alphabet’s return over 2023–2025 was 203.65%, and Pichai earned twice his target on the relevant award. The broader lesson is narrower than “management is against shareholders”: management has substantial money alongside them, but private-subsidiary awards require scrutiny of valuation and the capital used to produce growth.

blocks.heading: What have Alphabet's revenue and profit done in the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from $257,637 million in 2021 to $402,836 million in 2025. Growth slowed sharply after 2021, then recovered in 2024 and 2025. The latest quarters continued that recovery, with year-over-year growth reaching approximately 24% in June 2026.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Alphabet's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next expected results date is October 28, 2026. Management plans greater use of third-party capacity during the third quarter while its own facilities are built. Renting lets Google serve customers sooner, but it pays an outside provider while also paying for new infrastructure.

The trade can work if customers stay with Google and later move onto cheaper company-owned capacity. It becomes troubling if rental costs continue while Alphabet’s own equipment remains underused and depreciation rises. Results should therefore reveal not only Cloud sales, but also the cost of fulfilling them.
